During the main phase of the Tsentr-2026 (Center-2026) military exercise, the latest Izdeliye 347 ground-launched missile system, equipped with a modified Kh-39 Light Multipurpose Guided Missile (LMUR), was used at the Chebarkulsky training ground to strike artillery positions identified through aerial reconnaissance.
Izdeliye 347 is a Russian ground-launched, multipurpose precision-guided missile system derived from the LMUR (Izdeliye 305), which was originally developed for airborne deployment from combat helicopters such as the Mi-28NM and Ka-52M.

Earlier today, the IRGC blew up a building used by the People’s Fighters Front (PFF), a Balochi nationalist militant organization operating in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, eastern Iran.
The strike comes amid a significant increase in PFF military activity in recent days, with attacks and operations taking place almost daily in Zahedan and Iranshahr.

UAV operators from the First Division of the Nation’s Shield Forces (NSF) targeted an Ansar Allah pickup truck carrying more than 20 fighters with a mortar round dropped from a quadcopter or hexacopter in Bani Omar, Al-Shamayatayn District, Taiz Governorate.
Almost all of the fighters aboard the vehicle were reportedly killed instantly.
The Yemeni Armed Forces released footage showing airstrikes targeting Ansar Allah positions in Taiz Governorate.

Earlier, Royal Saudi Air Force (RSAF) airstrikes targeted Ansar Allah positions in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa.
One of the airstrikes is claimed to have targeted a military site in the Al-Sabain District.

An Ansar Allah combined missile and drone attack targeted a camp belonging to Presidential Leadership Council (PLC) forces and the Star Cement factory in Al-Buraiqah District, Aden Governorate, southern Yemen.
The number of casualties and the extent of material damage caused by the strikes remain unclear at this time.

Ukrainian sources published images of a new 32-element anti-jamming CRPA antenna reportedly being used in Russian drones.
According to reports, 20-element CRPA antennas are also being prepared for use, while production of 24-element antennas is planned to begin in 2027.
CRPA antennas are widely used in Russian precision-guided weapons and UAVs, including Iskander-M ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, Geran/Garpiya-A1 and Gerbera drones, UMPK glide-bomb kits, UMPB-5/UMPB-5R, and others.
Previously, 4-, 8-, 12-, and 16-element CRPA antennas had been observed, manufactured in both China and Russia, including the Kometa-M produced by VNIIR-Progress.
In late July, images also emerged of a Geran-2 piston-powered drone variant with an enlarged compartment for the CRPA antenna. Ukrainian sources speculated that this could have been preparation for integrating the new 32-element anti-jamming antenna.
